title: Commission into alleged temple attacks under the previous government
manifesto_text: Constitute a special commission to investigate and act against those the manifesto alleges were responsible for attacks on temples during the previous government's tenure.
assessment: Recorded as a commitment in the TDP-Jana Sena "Praja Galam" joint manifesto (2024). ManifestoWatch catalogues the promise as worded by the party and does not itself assert who was responsible for the events referenced; the allegations, and the attribution of blame to the previous government, are the manifesto's and not ManifestoWatch's. No delivery verdict is assigned, as any outcome depends on investigations and judicial or official findings. Status pending.

title: Implement Vision 2047 / Viksit Bharat measures in the state
manifesto_text: Take measures to fully implement in the state the initiatives under the Vision 2047 plan for building a Viksit Bharat.
assessment: On track (early stage). The government has articulated the 'Swarna Andhra Vision 2047' framework - a roughly USD 2.4 trillion economy goal with a ten-point action plan - with the P4 poverty-eradication programme designated its first action item (launched March 2025). The vision is in early operationalisation. Approved/government citation to be attached.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Incentives for agriculture-based food processing
manifesto_text: Provide large incentives for setting up agriculture-produce-based industries to raise farmers' income and promote employment.
assessment: On track. A new Food Processing Policy was among the six industrial policies cleared by Cabinet in October 2024, offering capital subsidies, technology-upgrade support, and waste-processing and quality-certification incentives. Approved/government citation for the policy GO to be attached.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Restore Brand AP and attract investment under a new industrial policy
manifesto_text: Restore Brand AP, attract large-scale domestic and foreign investment, and set up industries to raise state revenue and create jobs; under a new Industrial Policy, encourage modern technologies such as artificial intelligence and machine learning.
assessment: On track. The government rolled out a suite of '4.0' sectoral policies to attract investment back to Andhra Pradesh - Industrial Development, MSME, Food Processing, Electronics and Private Parks in October 2024, followed by IT and GCC, Textile/Apparel and Maritime policies in December 2024 - with stated targets of roughly Rs 30-40 lakh crore in investment and 20 lakh jobs over 2024-2029, explicitly framed as bringing industry back after units shifted out during 2019-24.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Kapu welfare: at least Rs 15,000 crore over five years
manifesto_text: Allocate at least Rs 15,000 crore over the next five years for Kapu welfare, in addition to general welfare schemes, and take measures for Kapu empowerment and development.
assessment: Major shortfall. The Kapu Welfare Corporation is operational and received roughly Rs 170 crore in 2024-25 (largely scholarship reimbursements), but this is far below the manifesto commitment of a Rs 15,000 crore Kapu corporation fund. Marked low-confidence on-track given the large gap between the corpus promised and the amount flowing. Approved/government citation to be attached.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Strengthen the Brahmin Corporation and credit society
manifesto_text: Strengthen the Brahmin Corporation and the Brahmin Cooperative Credit Society.
assessment: On track. The Brahmin Welfare Corporation is operational and received funding in 2024-25 (reported around Rs 9.20 crore, chiefly for scholarship reimbursements). Whether the dedicated credit/cooperative-society element has been delivered is not separately confirmed. Approved/government citation to be attached.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Adequate funding for the Arya Vysya Corporation
manifesto_text: Allocate adequate funds to the Arya Vysya Corporation.
assessment: On track. The Arya Vysya Welfare Corporation is operational and received funding in 2024-25 (reported around Rs 25.65 crore, chiefly for scholarship reimbursements). Approved/government citation to be attached.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Funding for Kamma, Reddy, Velama and other upper-caste corporations
manifesto_text: Allocate adequate funds to Kamma, Reddy, Velama and other upper-caste corporations and take measures for their empowerment and development.
assessment: On track. Welfare/finance corporations for economically weaker upper-caste communities (Kapu, EBC, Reddy, Kamma, Arya Vysya, Brahmin, Kshatriya) are established and were funded in 2024-25, primarily for Post-Matric Scholarship (RTF) reimbursements. Figures are from press reporting of Finance Department releases; an approved/government citation is to be attached.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Pay fees directly to colleges to release certificates
manifesto_text: Pay fees directly to colleges so students receive their certificates without difficulty.
assessment: Operating. Tuition-fee reimbursement (RTF) under the Post-Matric Scholarship programme is released directly to colleges on a quarterly basis (with the maintenance allowance, MTF, paid to students), confirming the direct-to-college payment mechanism, and funds are actively disbursed each academic year.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Digital health cards for every citizen
manifesto_text: Provide digital health cards to every citizen.
assessment: On track. Digital health records are being created statewide: ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) IDs and Electronic Health Records are being generated at scale (over 88% coverage in a sampled district), and the state's "Sanjeevani" universal-health initiative (with Tata and the Gates Foundation, first Digital Nerve Centre in Kuppam) is digitising the records of about 5 crore citizens and linking facilities on one platform.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Complete pucca houses for existing patta-holders
manifesto_text: Complete government construction of pucca houses for those who have already received sanctioned house pattas.
assessment: On track. Pucca-house construction for poor and kutcha-house households continues through the AP State Housing Corporation (APSHCL) and the central PMAY-G programme, complemented by the house-site patta drive above. Completion figures specifically attributable to the current government are not separately confirmed here.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: House-site land: 2 cents in towns, 3 cents in villages
manifesto_text: Allot 2 cents of land in towns and 3 cents in villages for house construction.
assessment: On track. Under the flagship "Housing for All" programme, the government issued GO Ms No. 23 (Revenue [Lands-I], dated 27 January 2025) with guidelines for distributing house-site pattas of 2-3 cents to homeless poor families in rural and urban areas, with eligibility tied to not already owning a house/site and an Aadhaar check.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Develop Visakhapatnam as a financial capital
manifesto_text: Develop Visakhapatnam as a financial capital.
assessment: On track. The government is actively positioning Visakhapatnam as a financial/technology hub - the Chief Minister has publicly committed to developing it as a fintech hub, and the state is courting major IT/AI investment (a Google AI hub, a proposed Quantum Valley, and engagement with firms such as Capgemini). The full "financial capital" designation remains aspirational and in progress.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Name Bhogapuram airport after Alluri Sitarama Raju
manifesto_text: Name the Bhogapuram airport as Alluri Sitarama Raju Airport.
assessment: Fulfilled. The new greenfield airport at Bhogapuram (near Visakhapatnam) carries the official name Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, honouring the freedom fighter - meeting the manifesto commitment on the airport's naming. (Airport construction itself is a GMR-led PPP nearing completion and is not scored here.)
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Cut electricity bills via rooftop solar
manifesto_text: Reduce household electricity bills by linking with the central government's rooftop solar power scheme and purchasing surplus power from the public.
assessment: On track. Andhra Pradesh is implementing the central PM Surya Ghar rooftop-solar scheme with state top-up subsidies - a 2 kW rooftop unit is fully free for SC/ST households (Centre Rs 60,000 + State Rs 55,000), with partial state support plus a bank loan for Backward Classes - and the Chief Minister set a target of about 2 million units (10,000 per Assembly constituency) for 2025, alongside 100% SGST reimbursement and model solar villages. Reported via The Hindu; direct approved/government citation to be attached.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Control liquor prices and ban toxic brands
manifesto_text: Control liquor prices and ban toxic liquor brands.
assessment: Delivered as policy. A new excise policy was cleared by Cabinet on 18 September 2024 and took effect in October 2024: it restored private retail, set affordable liquor priced from about Rs 99, allowed major IMFL brands, and was framed explicitly as a way to curb the spurious/illicit liquor trade that the government said had grown under the previous regime. It is a revenue-generating reform rather than the phased prohibition the party had previously favoured.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: State-wide skill census
manifesto_text: Conduct a state-wide skill census and use it to raise people's skill levels.
assessment: On track. The government ordered a statewide Skill Census via GO No. 13 (2024) to map the skills of the workforce against industry demand and identify skill gaps, and the exercise was carried out. Approved/government citation for the GO and outcomes to be attached.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Youth: 20 lakh jobs and a Rs 3,000/month unemployment allowance
manifesto_text: Provide 20 lakh jobs for youth over five years and a Rs 3,000 per month unemployment allowance to the unemployed.
assessment: Stalled. The Super Six pledge of 20 lakh jobs in five years with a Rs 3,000/month unemployment allowance (Yuva Galam) until employment has not been operationalised roughly 18 months into the term. Ministers have repeatedly said it will start "soon" (Nara Lokesh in June 2025, the Chief Minister in July 2025), but no scheme guidelines or notification have been issued and the promised 1 January job calendar was not notified. (Separate teacher recruitment via Mega DSC did proceed and is tracked under its own promise.) Approved/government citation to be attached.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: High Court bench in Kurnool
manifesto_text: Immediately set up a High Court bench in Kurnool.
assessment: Committed and in groundwork, not yet established. The Chief Minister announced in the Assembly (November 2024) the intent to set up a High Court bench at Kurnool, ministers reaffirmed it, and in January 2025 the Kurnool district administration was tasked with identifying land and infrastructure. A High Court bench requires central and judiciary processes and is not yet operational. Approved/government citation to be attached.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Gratuity for Anganwadi workers and higher ASHA minimum wage
manifesto_text: Pay gratuity to Anganwadi workers in line with the Supreme Court judgment, and take measures to raise the minimum wage for ASHA workers.
assessment: Delivered in part: in March 2025 Andhra Pradesh became the first state to grant gratuity to ASHA workers (a retirement benefit of about Rs 1.5 lakh for 30 years of service, covering ~42,752 workers), alongside maternity benefits (180-day leave counted as working days, worth up to Rs 60,000); the state also pays the country's highest ASHA honorarium at Rs 10,000/month. Gratuity for Anganwadi workers and helpers was announced on Women's Day, with a further honorarium hike flagged as forthcoming.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Organic farming (ZBNF) on 1000 acres per parliamentary seat
manifesto_text: Take up organic / Zero Budget Natural Farming on 1000 acres in each parliamentary constituency, with financial, cultivation and marketing support.
assessment: Andhra Pradesh's Community-managed Natural Farming (APCNF, formerly ZBNF), run by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha, continues as a large statewide programme. The current government is reported to be reassessing and refining natural-farming policy rather than expanding it, and the specific manifesto target of natural farming on 1,000 acres per parliamentary constituency is not separately confirmed. Approved/government citation to be attached.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: ID cards, welfare and crop insurance for tenant farmers
manifesto_text: Issue identity cards to tenant farmers, extend all welfare schemes to them, and provide crop insurance.
assessment: Crop Cultivator Rights Cards (CCRC) are being issued to tenant farmers, giving them recognised cultivation rights to register crops and access input subsidies, crop insurance and the Annadata Sukhibhava benefit. Caveats: many informal tenants without a CCRC remain excluded, and under Annadata the crop-insurance premium is now met by farmers from the aid. Approved/government citation to be attached.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: 90% subsidy for drip irrigation
manifesto_text: Provide a 90 percent subsidy for drip irrigation.
assessment: The Andhra Pradesh Micro Irrigation Project (APMIP) provides up to 90% subsidy on drip irrigation for small and marginal farmers (with lower slabs of 70% and 50% for larger holdings); the project remains active with 2025-26 district targets. This is a continuing scheme rather than a new introduction.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Establish the Visakhapatnam railway zone
manifesto_text: Establish a railway zone headquartered at Visakhapatnam and allocate suitable land immediately to realize it.
assessment: The South Coast Railway (SCoR) zone, headquartered at Visakhapatnam with four divisions (Guntakal, Guntur, Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam), was operationalised on 1 June 2026 per the gazette notification. This is primarily a central (Railway Ministry) action long sought by the state. An approved/government citation for the operationalisation is to be attached.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: P4 (Public-Private-People Partnership) poor-to-rich schemes
manifesto_text: Implement Public, Private and People's Partnership (P4) schemes aimed at making the poor prosperous.
assessment: Delivered: the P4 (Public-Private-People Partnership) / Margadarsi-Bangaru Kutumbam poverty-eradication programme was launched on 30 March 2025 under the Swarna Andhra Vision 2047, connecting affluent mentors (Margadarsi) with underprivileged families (Bangaru Kutumbam) via an app and portal. The government's role is facilitation rather than direct monetary support.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Continue building the capital Amaravati
manifesto_text: Continue construction of the people's capital Amaravati while developing all regions.
assessment: Construction of the Amaravati capital has resumed under the current government, with a fresh round of land pooling (around 20,494 acres) for key infrastructure, and the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2026 recognising Amaravati as the sole capital was passed by the Lok Sabha in April 2026.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Protect the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant
manifesto_text: Protect the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant.
assessment: Protected: the Union Cabinet approved a Rs 11,440 crore revival package for RINL / Visakhapatnam Steel Plant in January 2025 (Rs 10,300 crore fresh equity plus Rs 1,140 crore working-capital conversion), averting privatisation; RINL returned to profit (Rs 54 crore in January 2026). Long-term sustainability (captive iron-ore mines) remains debated.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: 3 free gas cylinders per household per year (Deepam-2)
manifesto_text: Provide 3 free gas cylinders per year to every household.
assessment: Delivered: Deepam-2 launched on 1 November 2024 - three free LPG cylinders per year (one every four months), subsidy credited within 48 hours of booking, at an estimated Rs 2,684 crore/year; second instalment disbursed April 2025.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Rapidly increase the state gross output
manifesto_text: Take strong measures to rapidly increase the state's gross domestic product.
assessment: Per the Andhra Pradesh Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 (the state government own report, tabled in the legislature with the budget), GSDP for 2024-25 was estimated at Rs 16.06 lakh crore - up from Rs 14.22 lakh crore - growing 9.24% at constant prices and 12.94% at current prices, against national rates of 6.4% and 9.7%. The government further reported GSDP growth of 11.28% in the second quarter of 2025-26, above the national average. By this official data the state output is rising faster than the national benchmark. Caveats: the figures are the state government own estimates, growth cannot be cleanly attributed to specific government measures, and the promise sets no defined target for "rapidly".
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

assessment: As of late 2025 the Rs 1,500/month payment to women aged 19-59 (Maha Shakti) had not been launched, even as other Super Six schemes were rolled out. Delivery pending; an approved-source citation confirming the non-launch is to be attached.

title: Rs 20,000/year financial assistance per farmer (Annadata Sukhibhava)
manifesto_text: Provide Rs 20,000 per year in financial assistance to every farmer.
assessment: Launched as Annadata Sukhibhava (replacing YSR Rythu Bharosa): Rs 20,000/year per farmer, comprising Rs 6,000 from the Centre under PM-KISAN plus Rs 14,000 from the state, disbursed in phases from August 2025. The opposition alleges eligibility criteria roughly halved the beneficiary count.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Rs 15,000/year per school-going child (Talliki Vandanam)

assessment: Launched in 2025 as Talliki Vandanam (replacing Amma Vodi): Rs 15,000/year per school-going child credited to mothers, covering ~67 lakh students with Rs 9,407 crore allocated for 2025-26. Rs 2,000 of the Rs 15,000 is deducted at source for school upkeep, and the opposition alleges beneficiary numbers were reduced from earlier estimates.
source_doc: Praja Galam - Ummadi (Joint) Manifesto 2024, TDP-Jana Sena

title: Reimburse GST and provide free power for weavers
manifesto_text: Reimburse GST on handloom products and provide 200 free electricity units per month to handloom weavers and 500 units to powerloom weavers.
assessment: The government launched a free-electricity scheme for weavers effective 1 April 2026, providing 200 free units per month to handloom weavers and 500 to powerloom weavers - matching the manifesto figures - benefiting about 93,000 handloom and 11,488 powerloom families, with roughly Rs 150 crore allocated annually. The free-power commitment is delivered; the separate handloom-products GST-reimbursement element is not yet confirmed.
